_: Trade classes (lane 2.6c1; decision 0141): what a merchant class stocks and buys, as item filters over items.json (kind, subkind, id prefix, value cap). A shop is a class and a culture, never a list; `always` names the few shelf ids a class carries on top of its drawn lines (the smith's bog iron and leather strips, which the slice's forge recipes start from). `settles` coin: the purse is the class's `purse` (its Skyrim VendorGold list, `purseFrom`) times economy.json `vendorPurse[placeTier]`, or the `purse` itself where `purseByTier` is false (a rich buyer); `atBase`: the class trades at item value, no barter band (Morrowind's rich creature merchants); goods: the trader holds no coin and pays in kind (settlement register section 7, villages barter tools, salt, sap, hide and worked craft). Read by worldgen.trade_tables into packages/economy/src/data/stock-tables.json.

classes.why: A general trader at a coin place: a broad shelf of everyday goods and plain arms. Buys almost anything. No picks or probes: those are the fence's line (decision 0151), sold by the salvage trade.
A bed-keeper or purser who sells a traveller food, drink and light. Buys provisions.

A salvage merchant on a wrecking coast: arms, gear, metal and trinkets off lost hulls. Buys the same. The coast's fence: held-back salvage changes hands here, so it sells picks and probes (decision 0151).
A village trader in kind: stocks what the village makes and uses (food, salt, sap, hide, tools, worked craft, plain cloth) and takes the same in exchange; no coin (settlement register section 7).
classes.purseFrom: none: a trader in kind pays in goods

classes.why: A smith: arms and armour, ore and ingots, the repair hammer; buys metal and arms.
classes.purseFrom: Skyrim VendorGoldBlacksmith 1000 (the city smith's list; VendorGoldBlacksmithTown 500 is the village smith, the village multiplier 0.5 of it)

classes.why: An apothecary: potions, ingredients and scrolls; buys ingredients and potions.

A rich buyer at Lilmoth's lighter moorings, which lie out of the tariff line: the Reed-Sail Compact's common purse buys whole cargoes off the deep-water hulls before they reach the quay, so it can take a costly piece at once. Trades at base value: it buys by the cargo, not by haggling.
classes.purseFrom: Morrowind's richest buyer (the Mudcrab merchant, 10,000) is 25 times the Trader median (400); 25 x the general trader's purse at the slice's village tier (750 x 0.5 = 375) = 9,375. Fixed, not scaled by tier, like Morrowind's.

classes.why: A rich buyer on the wrecking coast, off the cities on the Ashlander model: the stage office at Chasepoint keeps the salvage families' common chest and buys what the hulls give up whole. Trades at base value: it pays the families' rate, not a shop's.
classes.purseFrom: Creeper (5,000) is 12.5 times Morrowind's Trader median (400); 12.5 x the general trader's purse at the slice's village tier (750 x 0.5 = 375) = 4,687.5, rounded up. Fixed, not scaled by tier, like Morrowind's.
